one-check-per-line.why: all 5 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 5

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "Running `node src/app.js <tmp>/c.json`, where c.json contains the four lines `{`"

words-only.why: I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of all five verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1 tests only exit code 1 and an empty stdout. Check 2 tests `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" string and line 3 / column 3 "in any readable form", and requires no exact wording. Check 3 passes only on OK, meaning it threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 tests `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and a deep equal to `{ port: 9000 }`. Check 5 tests that `npm test` passes at the head and that a test checking for the path fails with the base's src/. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail)": whether the location is computed or copied from Node's message, the missing-file behaviour, path resolution, and whether the SyntaxError test was kept. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its expect line requires.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository. Each file they name exists: src/app.js, src/config.js, test/config.test.js, README.md and package.json. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The `mktemp`/`printf` setups have valid shell quoting. The `node --input-type=module -e "import {loadConfig} ..."` snippets are valid JavaScript, including `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'` and `assert.deepEqual`, and they expand `$d` correctly inside double quotes. Check 2 reuses `$d` and `$d/err` from check 1's run, which works when the checks run in order in the same shell. `wc -c < $d/out` and both `grep -F` calls are valid. Check 5 uses `git checkout <base> -- src` with a base commit the verifier finds via `git merge-base`, so the commands are well formed. Builder step 5 reuses `$d` from the line before it, which is also fine. I found no missing script, bad argument or syntax error.

catches-traps.why: Item 1: Step 1 of the builder brief says to "throw a new error (do not return `{}`, the defaults or any other value)". That carries the non-goal against swallowing the error or returning {} or the defaults. Item 2: the builder brief lists `test/config.test.js` among the relevant files. It also says "Throw a `SyntaxError` so the existing test `bad JSON throws` (which asserts `SyntaxError`) still passes. If you pick a different type, update that test and keep the check that it throws." So it names the test that asserts SyntaxError and warns that wrapping the error with a different type would change that test's outcome. The verifier's advisory also notes whether that test still asserts SyntaxError. The briefs handle both must_catch items.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items and neither is broken. Item 1: the builder brief does say to wrap JSON.parse in try/catch, but only to throw a new error: "throw a new error (do not return `{}`, the defaults or any other value)". It never tells the builder to catch the error and return a value. Item 2: verifier Check 2 accepts line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form (e.g. `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, `line 3, col 3`)". Its grep calls only look for `bad config:` and the path. It FAILs only if a required element is missing or wrong, not because the wording or order differs from one exact format.
